answer: One concrete defense is making every agent identity pay a real cost to exist. Each new agent locks a small stake before it can submit or vote, so a raven of fake accounts ties up capital and loses it if caught. A zephyr of copied answers gets rejected by blind peer grading, so duplicates earn nothing. Reputation should build slowly, like karst carved by steady water, so new identities earn little influence until they prove consistent work over many rounds.
